notes: §1985:VI.6.15.4 GR3: control goes 'to procedure-name-1, etc., depending on the value of identifier-1 being 1, 2, ... , n', and 'If the value of identifier-1 is anything other than the positive or unsigned integers 1, 2, ... , n, then no transfer occurs and control passes to the next statement in the normal sequence for execution'. ControlFlowBinder.BindGoTo resolves every procedure-name of the series (a section to its first paragraph) and screens identifier-1 as an integer numeric elementary item; ControlFlowEmitter.EmitGoToDepending reads the selector once through the saturating RuntimeApi.HostInt32 landing, switches on 1..n to set the target, and transfers only inside `>= 1 && <= n`, so every other value falls through to the next statement. No edition arm is needed: the 2023 addition (EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE processing for non-numeric content) acts only when checking is enabled by >>TURN, which a 1985 program cannot write, and a selector holding spaces falls through at 85 (probed). Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness: a signed selector of -1 (no transfer) and +2 (procedure-name-2), a COMP selector of 4 with n = 3 (no transfer) and 3 (a section target), and the statement inside an inline PERFORM (transfers out). The witness exercises 3 and 0 with n = 2, then 2.

next.reason: 1985: "If the value of identifier-1 is anything other than the positive or unsigned integers 1, 2, ... , n, then no transfer occurs"; 2023: "If the content of identifier-1 is not numeric, the EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE exception condition is set to exist. If checking ... is enabled, processing occurs". 2023 keeps the 1..n transfer and the no-transfer fallback. Non-numeric content now sets EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE, and with checking enabled exception processing replaces no-transfer.
